title: Book: The Black Swan — Nassim Nicholas Taleb (2007)
publisher: Artha Kavach original summary of a book's ideas (paraphrase, not a quotation; the author's opinion, not settled fact) — pending manual verification
text: Nassim Taleb argues that rare, unpredictable, high-impact events — black swans — drive a large share of history and markets, and that we invent tidy stories afterwards to make them look predictable. Money lessons: forecasts are often overconfident, so do not stake your survival on them; avoid ruin first, because one huge loss can end the game however good your average is; keep some exposure to safety and some to upside (his 'barbell' idea); and prefer being robust to being clever. In everyday terms this supports an emergency fund, adequate health and term cover, avoiding leverage, and not putting everything into one asset. Criticism: the tone is combative, and the book is more philosophy than a how-to.
